title: The Court That Never Was — Episode 3

characters.persona: the man who calls himself a judge
his first client, a man out of time
his clerk, hired to play court staff

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Five thousand rupees. That is what it costs to build a court in this country. One second-hand table. Eight inches of wood. One board with gold letters. And one girl who has never seen a courtroom in her life.
lines.spoken: Five thousand rupees. That is what it costs to build a court in this country. One second-hand table. Eight inches of wood. One board with gold letters. And one girl who has never seen a courtroom in her life.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Sir, my brother sold our father's sewing machines without asking me. I need an order before he sells the shop also.
lines.spoken: Sir, my brother sold our father's sewing machines without asking me. I need an order before he sells the shop also.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: Mine is a salary matter. Three months unpaid. Irfan is saying you finish quickly.
lines.spoken: Mine is a salary matter. Three months unpaid. Irfan is saying you finish quickly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I have not accepted either matter.
lines.spoken: I have not accepted either matter.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: They have come because the first order worked.
lines.spoken: They have come because the first order worked.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That was not an order.
lines.spoken: That was not an order.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Then write me the same kind of not-order.
lines.spoken: Then write me the same kind of not-order.

lines.speaker: SECOND MAN
lines.text: Five hundred I can pay now. Another five hundred after recovery.
lines.spoken: Five hundred I can pay now. Another five hundred after recovery.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: This is a public canteen. Put that money away.
lines.spoken: This is a public canteen. Put that money away.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: Then where should we put it? Irfan said your office is upstairs.
lines.spoken: Then where should we put it? Irfan said your office is upstairs.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: I said he works upstairs. I did not say he has an office.
lines.spoken: I said he works upstairs. I did not say he has an office.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Bas. Both of you, wait till evening. Bring every agreement, receipt and notice you are having.
lines.spoken: Bas. Both of you, wait till evening. Bring every agreement, receipt, and notice you are having.

lines.speaker: FIRST MAN
lines.text: And where will you hear us, sir?
lines.spoken: And where will you hear us, sir?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You will be informed.
lines.spoken: You will be informed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He did not take the envelopes on the table. He took them under it. Where dignity could pretend not to see.
lines.spoken: He did not take the envelopes on the table. He took them under it — where dignity could pretend not to see.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Five days after a stranger touched his feet, Mervyn Aloysius Fonseca climbed a metal staircase above a tyre shop.
lines.sfx_cue: air wrench bursts, metal staircase creaking
lines.spoken: Five days after a stranger touched his feet, Mervyn Aloysius Fonseca climbed a metal staircase above a tyre shop.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Mind the second step. It bends when heavy people are using it.
lines.spoken: Mind the second step. It bends when heavy people are using it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You said the room has a separate entrance.
lines.spoken: You said the room has a separate entrance.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: It is having. Nobody enters through the tyres unless they fall through the floor.
lines.spoken: It is having. Nobody enters through the tyres unless they fall through the floor.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There is grease on the wall.
lines.spoken: There is grease on the wall.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Downstairs also there is grease. That is how a tyre shop is earning money.
lines.spoken: Downstairs also there is grease. That is how a tyre shop is earning money.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Clients must be able to wait outside.
lines.spoken: Clients must be able to wait outside.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Clients? You told me typing work.
lines.spoken: Clients? You told me typing work.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Documentation. Consultations. Settlement of private disputes.
lines.spoken: Documentation. Consultations. Settlement of private disputes.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Advocate work?
lines.spoken: Advocate work?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No.
lines.spoken: No.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Write the receipt.
lines.spoken: Write the receipt.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Occupation?
lines.spoken: Occupation?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Dispute resolution.
lines.spoken: Dispute resolution.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: That is not an occupation.
lines.spoken: That is not an occupation.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It is now.
lines.spoken: It is now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By noon, one carpenter had put a second-hand dining table on a platform eight inches high. Not one foot. Eight inches. Enough to look up at. Cheap enough to afford.
lines.spoken: By noon, one carpenter had put a second-hand dining table on a platform eight inches high. Not one foot. Eight inches. Enough to look up at. Cheap enough to afford.

lines.speaker: CARPENTER
lines.text: If you lean on the left side, the whole thing will salute you.
lines.spoken: If you lean on the left side, the whole thing will salute you.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Brace it underneath.
lines.spoken: Brace it underneath.

lines.speaker: CARPENTER
lines.text: That is costing two hundred more.
lines.spoken: That is costing two hundred more.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It costs nothing if you had built it straight.
lines.spoken: It costs nothing if you had built it straight.

lines.speaker: CARPENTER
lines.text: Straight wood is costing more than crooked wood, sir.
lines.spoken: Straight wood is costing more than crooked wood, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Do it.
lines.spoken: Do it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At two o'clock, a sign painter carried in a black board with gold letters.
lines.spoken: At two o'clock, a sign painter carried in a black board with gold letters.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution Forum. Exactly as you have written.
lines.spoken: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution Forum. Exactly as you have written.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The word forum is smaller than the others.
lines.spoken: The word forum is smaller than the others.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: You paid for twenty-four letters. This is having thirty-seven.
lines.spoken: You paid for twenty-four letters. This is having thirty-seven.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And the line below?
lines.spoken: And the line below?

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: Presiding Officer. That is large enough to read from the tyre shop.
lines.spoken: Presiding Officer. That is large enough to read from the tyre shop.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Make sir smaller.
lines.spoken: Make sir smaller.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: There is no sir on the board.
lines.spoken: There is no sir on the board.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I said officer. Make officer smaller.
lines.spoken: I said— officer. Make officer smaller.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He was thinking that word so loudly, it came out of his mouth.
lines.spoken: He was thinking that word so loudly, it came out of his mouth.

lines.speaker: SIGN PAINTER
lines.text: You said— never mind. Give me fifty rupees for correction.
lines.spoken: You said— never mind. Give me fifty rupees for correction.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Hang it straight first.
lines.spoken: Hang it straight first.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: What is this board?
lines.spoken: What is this board?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It states the work conducted here.
lines.spoken: It states the work conducted here.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: You told me typing.
lines.spoken: You told me typing.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Documents will be typed.
lines.spoken: Documents will be typed.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Police will come for dispute resolution?
lines.spoken: Police will come for dispute resolution?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Only if tyres are sold without receipts.
lines.spoken: Only if tyres are sold without receipts.

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Your board is very handsome, sir. Please conduct all resolutions upstairs.
lines.spoken: Your board is very handsome, sir. Please conduct all resolutions upstairs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That was the first time the tyre shop owner called him sir. Mervyn paid the sign painter without bargaining.
lines.spoken: That was the first time the tyre shop owner called him sir. Mervyn paid the sign painter without bargaining.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: A dais? You have bought a dais before buying groceries?
lines.spoken: A dais? You have bought a dais before buying groceries?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There is rice for three days.
lines.spoken: There is rice for three days.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: There is rice. There is no oil. There is no dal. But somewhere above a tyre shop, there is a dais.
lines.spoken: There is rice. There is no oil. There is no dal. But somewhere above a tyre shop, there is a dais.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It is an office expense.
lines.spoken: It is an office expense.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Say the office name properly.
lines.spoken: Say the office name properly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution Forum.
lines.spoken: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution Forum.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: And who appointed you to it?
lines.spoken: And who appointed you to it?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Private parties appoint an arbitrator by consent.
lines.spoken: Private parties appoint an arbitrator by consent.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Did these parties consent?
lines.spoken: Did these parties consent?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: They brought files and fees.
lines.spoken: They brought files and fees.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: That is not what I asked you.
lines.spoken: That is not what I asked you.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The record will reflect consent.
lines.spoken: The record will reflect consent.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: What record?
lines.spoken: What record?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The one I am creating.
lines.spoken: The one I am creating.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: And who is keeping this record?
lines.spoken: And who is keeping this record?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: A clerk.
lines.spoken: A clerk.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: You are having a clerk now?
lines.spoken: You are having a clerk now?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I will have one tomorrow.
lines.spoken: I will have one tomorrow.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: With whose salary?
lines.spoken: With whose salary?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The forum's fees.
lines.spoken: The forum's fees.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Mervyn. Look at me. Is this a court?
lines.spoken: Mervyn. Look at me. Is this a court?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. It is a lawful private forum.
lines.spoken: No. It is a lawful private forum.

lines.speaker: vaishali
lines.text: Then why is it needing a dais?
lines.spoken: Then why is it needing a dais?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Because people obey a raised table.
lines.spoken: Because people obey a raised table.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, I was told there is a clerk vacancy?
lines.spoken: Sir, I was told there is a clerk vacancy?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Who told you?
lines.spoken: Who told you?

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: The sign painter, sir. He is my mother's neighbour. He said you paid on time.
lines.spoken: The sign painter, sir. He is my mother's neighbour. He said you paid on time.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Have you worked in an office before?
lines.spoken: Have you worked in an office before?

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: No, sir. Twelfth standard I finished. I can read English, type slowly, and make tea quickly.
lines.spoken: No, sir. Twelfth standard I finished. I can read English, type slowly, and make tea quickly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Tea is not part of the designation.
lines.spoken: Tea is not part of the designation.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: There is a designation?
lines.spoken: There is a designation?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Registry clerk.
lines.spoken: Registry clerk.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Registry... like a court registry?
lines.spoken: Registry… like a court registry?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Like a private forum registry.
lines.spoken: Like a private forum registry.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Will I have to wear a uniform, sir?
lines.spoken: Will I have to wear a uniform, sir?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. Plain clothes. Clean file work. You will maintain the register and call matters by number.
lines.spoken: No. Plain clothes. Clean file work. You will maintain the register and call matters by number.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: I don't... I have never called a matter, sir.
lines.spoken: I don't… I have never called a matter, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Say — matter number one, parties to enter.
lines.spoken: Say: matter number one, parties to enter.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Matter number one, parties to enter.
lines.spoken: Matter number one… parties to enter.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Louder. People waiting near an air compressor must hear you.
lines.spoken: Louder. People waiting near an air compressor must hear you.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Matter number one, parties to enter!
lines.spoken: Matter number one, parties to enter!

lines.speaker: TYRE SHOP OWNER
lines.text: Very respectable. Even my customers are frightened.
lines.spoken: Very respectable. Even my customers are frightened.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: What is the salary, sir?
lines.spoken: What is the salary, sir?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Three thousand rupees per month. Paid on the last working day.
lines.spoken: Three thousand rupees per month. Paid on the last working day.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Three thousand... every month?
lines.spoken: Three thousand… every month?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: If the register is correct.
lines.spoken: If the register is correct.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: My father is getting two thousand six hundred, sir. Night security.
lines.spoken: My father is getting two thousand six hundred, sir. Night security.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your father's salary is not before this forum.
lines.spoken: Your father's salary is not before this forum.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sorry, sir.
lines.spoken: Sorry, sir.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Read this appointment acknowledgment. Sign at the bottom.
lines.spoken: Read this appointment acknowledgment. Sign at the bottom.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: It is saying... I certify the proceedings recorded by me.
lines.spoken: It is saying… I certify the proceedings recorded by me.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That is standard language.
lines.spoken: That is standard language.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: What proceedings, sir?
lines.spoken: What proceedings, sir?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The matters you call. The appearances. The documents filed.
lines.spoken: The matters you call. The appearances. The documents filed.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: And if I am spelling something wrong?
lines.spoken: And if I am spelling something wrong?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You correct it before signing.
lines.spoken: You correct it before signing.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: My mother will not believe this. Nobody in our family has ever had a desk job.
lines.spoken: My mother will not believe this. Nobody in our family has ever had a desk job.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then give her something respectable to believe.
lines.spoken: Then give her something respectable to believe.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At four thirty, Sarika Kamble opened a new register. Mervyn wrote one on the first page, and two on the second.
lines.spoken: At four thirty, Sarika Kamble opened a new register. Mervyn wrote one on the first page, and two on the second.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Nobody knows this address yet.
lines.spoken: Nobody knows this address yet.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: The two matters are finished for today, sir.
lines.spoken: The two matters are finished for today, sir.

lines.speaker: STRANGER
lines.text: I am not one of the two.
lines.spoken: I am not one of the two.

lines.speaker: STRANGER
lines.text: I need the presiding officer.
lines.spoken: I need the presiding officer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two days that board had been hanging. Two days. And already, somebody had come who was not sent.
lines.spoken: Two days that board had been hanging. Two days. And already, somebody had come who was not sent.
